plain_token.title: {name}: the irrigationd token is sent in plain text
plain_token.description: irrigationd on {name} doesn't support TLS yet, so Home Assistant sends the token in plain text, where anyone watching the network can read it. Update irrigationd on the controller and reinstall it with `sudo make install`. Home Assistant switches to TLS by itself within an hour, and this notice goes away. Then add `IRRIGATIOND_PLAIN_TOKEN=no` to `/etc/default/irrigationd` and restart irrigationd. Until then, you can turn off **Allow the token in plain text** under **Configure** to stop it being sent at all, but this controller will be unreachable until irrigationd is updated.

plain_token_old_python.title: {name}: the irrigationd token is sent in plain text
plain_token_old_python.description: This version of Home Assistant can't use TLS with a pre-shared key, so the irrigationd token on {name} is sent in plain text, where anyone watching the network can read it. Update Home Assistant to 2025.2 or later, and this notice goes away once {name} connects over TLS. Until then, keep `IRRIGATIOND_PLAIN_TOKEN=yes` on the controller.

master_switch_stuck.title: The master switch {switch} didn't turn off
master_switch_stuck.description: Home Assistant tried to turn off {switch}, the master valve or pump for irrigation, and it failed. If it's a pump, it may be running against closed valves. Check it now and turn it off by hand. This notice goes away the next time it turns off.

short_token.title: {name}: the irrigationd token is short
short_token.description: The token for {name} is shorter than 16 characters. Anyone who records one connection could try guesses against it offline. Generate a new one on the controller with `openssl rand -hex 16`, put it in `/etc/default/irrigationd`, restart irrigationd, then enter it under **Configure**. This notice goes away once the token is long enough.
